agentic.prompt:
Write a complete, runnable Python program using `pygame` that simulates a long-running autonomous service - a self-healing 'warehouse robot fleet' controller. Open a window and simulate a warehouse grid (e.g. 60x40 cells) with a fleet of 12 robots. Each robot must autonomously: pick up items from a spawn zone, carry them along its path to a delivery dock, avoid other robots and obstacles, and periodically encounter random failures (e.g. 5% per tick a robot reports 'fault' and must self-heal by re-routing after a short cooldown). The controller must demonstrate LONG-RUNNING RESILIENCE: track per-robot uptime and deliveries, log events to a rotating ring buffer (keep the last 200 events), and keep operating without user input for the whole run. Render robots as colored squares, items as small circles, docks as distinct markers, and a HUD with total deliveries, active faults, mean uptime, and the event-buffer size. Include a game loop handling QUIT. This benchmark runs the simulation for an extended window, so performance and stable long-run behavior (no unbounded memory growth, no crashes after thousands of ticks) matter.
Design note (interpret freely): the defining trait is autonomous resilience - the system must keep running through repeated random failures, log them, self-heal, and maintain a bounded memory footprint over a long horizon.
SCORING & STATS (REQUIRED): the program MUST persist a run summary to a local JSON file (e.g. fleet_stats.json) on shutdown (or every N ticks): total deliveries, total faults handled, mean robot uptime percent, and longest single uninterrupted run. This file must survive restarts.
SUCCESS CRITERIA: the program must (1) run top-to-bottom and open a visible window, (2) simulate 12 robots performing autonomous pickup/transport with collision avoidance, (3) handle random faults via self-healing re-route with no crashes, (4) maintain a bounded event ring buffer, (5) persist fleet stats to a JSON file. A simulation that crashes on the first fault or leaks memory fails.
